m:saobento: Entry to the azulejo hall is free, because it's the concourse of a working station: I haven't checked the exact hours (to be checked). The City Hall and the avenue can be seen from outside.
m:lello: Open every day 9am–7:30pm (official website, read on 12 October 2026); according to guides closed on 1 January, Easter, 1 May, 24 June and 25 December. The ticket is a voucher you can use to buy a book: the base price was €8 in September 2024 (Time Out), it may be different today: check on livrarialello.pt. Buy it online for a set time (valid up to 60 minutes after), otherwise there's a long queue. Backpacks and large bags aren't allowed.
m:clerigos: Tower and museum ticket: guides give €8–10 (€10 according to e-konomista.pt, June 2025; about €8 according to dicadeportugal.com, August 2026); free up to age 10: check on torredosclerigos.pt. Usual hours 9am–7pm, last entry 6:30pm (an undated guide). There's no lift. According to guides the church nave is free to visit.
m:bolsa: Palácio da Bolsa €14 (students and seniors €9.50; accompanied children under 12 free; dicadeportugal.com, updated August 2026). Guided tours only, at fixed times, in Portuguese, Spanish, French and English: arrive 10 minutes early, because latecomers aren't let in (Visit Porto website). Approximate hours: April to October about 9am–7pm, November to March 9am–1pm and 2–6pm: check on palaciodabolsa.com. Igreja de São Francisco: €9 (visitporto.travel); open about 9am–8pm, but November to February 9am–6pm.
m:ribeira: Free to walk. To go up to the upper part of the city there's the Guindais funicular (about €3 a ride, not covered by the Andante; April 2026 guide, to be checked) or the steep steps. Metro line D and pedestrians cross the bridge's upper deck: the wind can be strong. The restaurants with menus outside on the quay are the most expensive.
m:se: The church is mostly free to visit; the ticket for the cloister and other parts costs about €3 (portoalities.com, 2020 and 2023: to be checked). Approximate hours: 9am–6:30pm from April to October, 9am–5:30pm from November to March; closed at Christmas and Easter.
m:gaia: Prices and hours from portoalities.com (April 2026), to be checked on the cellars' websites: Taylor's €25 with audio guide and two wines, open 10am–7pm (last visit 6pm); Cálem from about €22, 10am–7pm; Graham's from €30, 10am–5:30pm April to October and a little earlier in winter; Ferreira from about €23, 10am–12:30pm and 2–6pm. Book online from April to October and at weekends: tours in English sell out first. Walk across the bridge's lower deck (about 15 minutes from the Ribeira). The Gaia cable car costs about €6–10 according to the sources, which disagree: check on gaiacablecar.com; it stops in strong wind.
m:bolhao: Free entry. Hours from the market website: Monday–Friday 8am–8pm, Saturday 8am–6pm; closed on Sundays and public holidays. The restaurants on the upper floor stay open until midnight (Monday–Saturday). The fish and fruit stalls are liveliest in the morning.
m:serralves: Full ticket (museum, villa, park, cinema house) €24; park only €15 (eurodicas.com.br and dicadeportugal.com, updated August 2026). From October to March: Monday–Friday 10am–6pm, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10am–7pm; from April to September one hour longer. Closed on 25 December and 1 January; on 24 and 31 December it closes at 4pm. According to the metropolitan area's tourism portal (iPorto) there's no weekly closing day; some guides mention closing on Monday or Tuesday, so check on serralves.pt. Until January 2027 there are exhibitions by Jenny Holzer, Lee Ufan and Alice Neel (dn.pt).
vd:padaria: A bakery and pâtisserie open since 1878, a short walk from the Torre dos Clérigos: pastéis de nata, almond sweets, savouries like shrimp rissóis and good coffee, at the counter or at little tables.
vp:padaria: A coffee with a pastel de nata is around €2–3 (menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:piolho: The students' café, open since 1909 opposite the university, between the Torre dos Clérigos and the Cordoaria gardens: sandwiches, francesinha, cachorrinho and beer at low prices, in the atmosphere of an old neighbourhood café. Open until late.
vp:piolho: A sandwich or a simple dish usually stays under €10 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:conga: Porto's home of the bifana: a roll with a slice of pork slow-cooked in a spicy sauce, served hot and dripping. A simple, noisy place on two floors, full of locals; the lunchtime queue moves fast.
vp:conga: A bifana costs about €3.50 and a small beer €1.50 (May 2026 guide). Closed on Sundays.
vd:candelabro: A bookshop-café that has become an evening haunt for locals, on a little square near Praça Carlos Alberto: old books on the walls, wine by the glass at honest prices, small plates and good music.
vp:candelabro: A glass of wine with a small plate is around €6–12 (menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:santiago: The most famous place for the francesinha, Porto's signature sandwich: bread, steak, sausage and ham, covered in melted cheese and a spicy beer-and-tomato sauce, often with an egg on top and chips. One portion is almost enough for two.
vp:santiago: A francesinha usually costs €12–16 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays; there's often a queue at dinnertime.
vd:guedes: The tavern of the pernil sandwich, thinly sliced roast pork leg, on its own or with Serra da Estrela sheep's cheese. Eat at the tables or on the square; there are also hot dishes and northern cured meats.
vp:guedes: The classic pernil sandwich costs about €5–6 (May 2026 guide). The starters brought to the table are charged: if you don't want them, send them back.
vd:majestic: Porto's historic café, opened in 1921 on the pedestrian shopping street: rooms with mirrors, gilded stucco and marble tables, sometimes with a piano. You come for the atmosphere: it's much more expensive than average.
vp:majestic: A coffee with milk comes to about €7 and a pastry with coffee goes over €10 (recent reviews, menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:bolhaoconf: A historic 1896 pâtisserie next to the market, always full of locals: egg sweets, bolas de Berlim, pastéis de bacalhau and toast. Choose at the counter, get a ticket and pay at the till by the door.
vp:bolhaoconf: A coffee with a pastry stays under €5 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:padeirinha: A neighbourhood pâtisserie between the Sé and Batalha, frequented by locals: generous pastéis de nata, toast, eggs and coffee at low prices, and francesinha at lunch too.
vp:padeirinha: A coffee with a pastel de nata is around €2–3 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:cantina32: An informal restaurant on Rua das Flores, the pedestrian street running down to the Ribeira: reinvented Portuguese dishes to share, like whole octopus, grilled squid and a house francesinha. It fills up fast: arrive at opening time or book.
vp:cantina32: Pricier than the taverns: with starters and a main you usually spend €20–30 per person (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:adega: A traditional tavern in a stepped alley above the Ribeira quay, with outdoor tables and a view of the bridge: grilled sardines and sea bass, octopus fillets with rice, salt cod. There's usually a queue at dinner.
vp:adega: A dish usually costs around €12–18 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays.
vd:saogoncalo: A small neighbourhood tavern in Gaia, ten minutes' walk from the cellars and away from the touristy riverside: sandwiches with house-cured ham, prego, cheese and charcuterie boards and the house wine, among locals.
vp:saogoncalo: A sandwich or a board with a glass of wine is around €8–12 (reviews, menu not seen). Open Tuesday to Saturday, only until 7:30pm.
vd:toca: A very narrow neighbourhood restaurant, a few steps from the Casa da Música: three fixed Portuguese dishes every day, generous portions, a carafe of wine and almost all local customers. Cash only.
vp:toca: A dish of the day usually stays under €10–12 (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays; cash only.
vd:rotunda: A traditional grill house on the big Boavista roundabout, frequented mostly by locals: picanha, ribs, chargrilled chicken and salt cod, with rice, black beans and salad. Single portions are big.
vp:rotunda: A grilled dish usually costs around €10–16 (menu not seen). The appetisers brought to the table are charged.
cd:seiponti: Fifty minutes on the Douro river under the city's bridges.
cd:teleferico: The cable car between the Luís I Bridge and the cellars: views of the river and of Porto.
cd:casamusica: Rem Koolhaas's concert hall and its auditoriums, explored with a guide.
cd:soaresreis: Portugal's oldest art museum, in a neoclassical palace.
cd:secloister: The cathedral's Gothic cloister with its azulejo panels.
cd:carmo: The side façade covered in blue azulejos, and the catacombs.
cd:tram: The story of Porto's tram, with vintage cars.
cd:sealife: An aquarium by the sea, near Foz.
cx:sealife: It's in Matosinhos, about 6 km from the centre.
